newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: US to push for communications services deal in WTO.
newsitem.headline: US to push for communications services deal in WTO.

text.p: The United States wlll push for wider support for a communications services agreement (CSA) at the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) ministerial meeting in Singapore next week, U.S. Federal Communications Commission chairman Reed Hundt said on Monday.

The agreement aims at opening the telecom industry of each WTO member-country to foreign competition, allowing interconnection among telephone companies, and opening the domestic market to foreign satellite services.
The United States has been lobbying for the liberalisation of telecommunications industry which involves more than $550 billion in total investments.

"What we want to do in Singapore a week from today...is to see all the countries that are sitting around the table willing to do as a group just what you have done in the Philippines," Hundt told reporters.
The Philippines recently opened up its industry to foreign companies and has allowed interconnection among the new entrants with the major telecom company.
Hundt said the United States, together with its allies such as the Philippines, Hong Kong and Japan, would convince other countries to agree to the core principles of the agreement.
At present, there are 48 countries which have made different levels of commitments. However, he said the commitments were not enough to form a critical mass.
"We simply have to have enough countries that are participating to make this a success," he said. He specifically wanted Malaysia and Indonesia to commit to such endeavours.
The proponents have until February next year to come up with an agreement.

Hundt said his government would not sign any agreement which fell short of its expectations but declined to give specifics. "We've said before, and I'll say again, we will not sign a bad deal," he said.
"I don't know as I stand here tonight whether to be optimistic or to be pessimistic. We just have to find out what does happen."
